step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture illustrates Raiffeisen Bank International's (RBI) integration between an on-premises Thales Key Management System (KMS) and AWS. The architecture is divided into two primary workflows: Onboarding and Key Management/Encryption Lifecycle. First, the Security DevOps Team pushes a mappings.json file to Git, which triggers a Git Action uploading the artifact into an S3 Artifacts Bucket. This S3 event invokes AWS Step Functions, which creates IAM roles in target accounts and triggers a Lambda function to provision a virtual tenant in the Thales On-Premises KMS. Upon completion, Step Functions triggers SNS to notify the Security DevOps Team. For key operations, the Product DevOps Team creates master keys on Thales On-Premises KMS. Thales uses the assumed IAM role to import/sync keys into AWS KMS. AWS KMS then generates Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) to encrypt data stored in S3 Data Storage and EBS volumes.

graph.name: RBI On-Premises Thales KMS Integration with AWS KMS
graph.notes: Hybrid key management architecture enabling on-premises control over encryption keys used across AWS services.

nodes.name: Security DevOps Team
nodes.notes: Initiates onboarding by pushing mapping configuration files and receives workflow completion notifications.

nodes.name: Git
nodes.notes: Version control repository hosting mapping JSON configuration and running deployment workflows.

nodes.name: S3 Artifacts Bucket
nodes.notes: Stores uploaded mapping configuration artifacts to trigger onboarding state machine.

nodes.name: Step Functions
nodes.notes: Orchestrates tenant onboarding by configuring IAM roles, invoking Lambda, and triggering notifications.

nodes.name: SNS
nodes.notes: Publishes notification upon successful virtual tenant onboarding.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Executes logic to establish and configure the virtual tenant inside Thales KMS.

nodes.name: Thales On-Premises KMS
nodes.notes: On-premises HSM/KMS holding master keys (CMK) and running virtual tenant wrappers.

nodes.name: IAM
nodes.notes: Role assumed by Thales to execute key management operations across target AWS accounts.

nodes.name: KMS
nodes.notes: AWS KMS holding virtual wrapper keys (master key and data key combined) for service encryption.

nodes.name: S3 Data Storage
nodes.notes: Stores application data encrypted using KMS Data Encryption Keys.

nodes.name: EBS
nodes.notes: Stores block volumes encrypted using KMS Data Encryption Keys.

nodes.name: Product DevOps Team
nodes.notes: Generates 256-bit symmetric encryption keys on Thales and manages key lifecycle/revocation.

edges.notes: Security DevOps Team pushes mappings.json into Git repository.
Git Action uploads mapping artifact into S3 Artifacts Bucket.
Artifact upload in S3 triggers Step Functions onboarding state machine.
Step Functions provisions IAM roles in target AWS accounts.
Step Functions triggers Lambda execution for tenant creation.
Lambda creates virtual tenant wrapper in Thales On-Premises KMS.
Step Functions triggers SNS notification upon successful onboarding completion.
SNS notifies Security DevOps Team that team is onboarded.
Thales On-Premises KMS assumes IAM role to operate in AWS.
Product DevOps Team generates 256-bit symmetric master key on Thales KMS.
Thales KMS syncs/imports key into AWS KMS as customer managed key wrapper.
AWS KMS uses Data Encryption Key (DEK) to encrypt S3 Data Storage bucket.
AWS KMS uses Data Encryption Key (DEK) to encrypt EBS storage volumes.
